This does NOT fit the LG WM2277HS, despite the product description.

My washer does NOT have a drain port at the 6:00 position of the gasket, however, this item DOES. There is a hole at 6:00 hidden underneath the folds of the gasket. As a result, it does NOT work. SO, the drain port has nothing to do with the other attachments or the "port" or fenestrations also at the 6:00 position on the OEM gasket (4986ER0004). Notice, no letter at the end of the OEM product number. THE PRODUCT DESCRIPTION IS INCOMPLETE (or LG has changed the gasket and drain system since this unit was purchased in 2006). -F implies drain port. -B is for no drain port.

Works great but the key is how long it lasts. The original element lasted 23.5 years, and a replacement I purchased from partselect.com costs twice as much and worked for only 4.5 years. This part took about 10 minutes to install and wll you need is a medium/large Philips screwdriver, a flashlight (or head light) and maybe a pair of pliers:
- turn off circuit breaker for range
- remove the 2 screws in the back plate
- gently pull element forward until attached wires stick out about 4 inches
- grab the gold colored clip at the end of each wire and gently pull to remove from element (may need pliers-I just use my hands); be sure to pull on the clips and not on the wires - if you pull a wire out of the clip you will be in deep do-do
- slide clips onto new element and push all the way on
- push element straight back so wires go through the back of the oven
- replace the two screws and turn power back on

My old whirlpool oven needed a new element. Thanks to Youtube videos this seemed like an easy fix. I searched the websites of the big box hard ware stores and really had no luck finding this item. I found it easily on Amazon. Once I got the Bake Element I blocked off the better part of my Saturday morning to this repair work. I got all the needed tools out, cut the breaker off, and set to work. Darn if I was not done in about 10 minutes. And once I cut the oven on this element glowed orange and heated up my oven in no time. My wife was so happy she credited me the whole morning's time and I was able to watch a bunch of college football. I love a job that turns out to be easier than you think.

It was not a match with my existing element.  The prongs the wires plug onto are twice and long as the original part so the new one would not go all the way back into back of the oven. So it would not fit.  My fault.  I should have just returned it. But instead I tried to move the plate on it back, but I could not get it to move back.  It is apparently welded to the element and won't move.  So I buggered it up to where it was not in resalable condition.  So I just ate it.  I will have to go somewhere and buy one in person so I can see it and make sure it fits.
